taxon_term.notes: Betaproteobacteria capable of dissimilatory vanadium reduction in contaminated mine environments. While not specifically reported in the Panzhihua tailings studies reviewed, Polaromonas is a well-established V(V)-reducing organism in circumneutral pH vanadium mine tailings in northern China and likely present in Panzhihua tailings based on similar environmental conditions (circumneutral pH 6.5-7.5, moderate temperature, high vanadium concentrations). Polaromonas performs dissimilatory V(V) reduction to V(IV) using c-type cytochromes (cymA, omcA) and membrane-associated nitrate reductases (narG). The organism couples oxidation of organic electron donors (lactate, acetate) to V(V) reduction, decreasing vanadium solubility by 2-3 orders of magnitude through precipitation of V(IV) species. This metabolic capacity is critical for vanadium immobilization during anaerobic microsites in revegetated tailings. Polaromonas also reduces Fe(III), Mn(IV), and As(V), contributing to polymetallic redox cycling in V-Ti tailings.

One isolate was identified as R. pisi, demonstrating the promiscuity of rhizobial-legume associations under metal stress conditions. R. pisi contributes to nitrogen enrichment of tailings soil through symbiotic nitrogen fixation and produces plant growth-promoting substances including IAA.
